framing: CBT-informed peer replies — preference-matched support that reinforces noticing, validation, gentle perspective-taking, or optional small actions. Peers are not CBT therapists.
source_note: Original templates informed by directional/nondirectional peer-support and peer+structured-prompt literature (docs/cbt-informed-research.md).

listening.norm: Reflect feelings/situation; do not advise or reframe unless asked.

shared_experience.norm: Share a similar noticing moment; optional tiny coping example — not fixing them.

practical_ideas.norm: Offer one optional inch-sized idea (BA-lite or balanced take); take-or-leave.

gentle_accountability.norm: Invite one tiny chosen step and a soft later check-in — no pressure.

encouragement.norm: Affirm showing up and noticing; avoid toxic positivity or 'just think positive'.

hints.listening: naming what feels heaviest without solving it yet
hints.shared_experience: pausing to notice situation / thought / feeling before pushing on
hints.practical_ideas: writing one next inch-sized step only
hints.gentle_accountability: choosing one tiny step to revisit later
hints.encouragement: treating noticing itself as a worthwhile step

listening: Hearing you on {summary}. I'm with you in noticing how hard that feels — no advice from me unless you want it.
Thanks for naming {summary}. Sitting with the feeling/situation with you, without trying to fix it.
shared_experience: I've had a stretch like that. What helped a little was {hint} — not a fix, just something that made it 5% more manageable.
You're not alone in this. When I was in something similar, noticing the situation vs the story in my head took a bit of pressure off.
practical_ideas: One optional idea, take or leave: {hint}. Only if it feels doable.
If useful: pick one balanced way to describe the same facts, or one tiny next action — skip either if it doesn't fit.
gentle_accountability: If you want, choose one tiny step for later and we can gently ask how it went next time — no pressure either way.
No push from me. If you pick one small action around {summary}, I'm happy to check in softly later.
encouragement: You're showing up and noticing {summary} — that already counts. Kindness to yourself here is allowed.
It's okay that this feels heavy. Taking a moment to notice it matters; you don't have to be 'fixed' today.
